questions.q: What are the three categories of error this lesson names, and which one does this lesson focus on?
options: Network errors, memory errors, and syntax errors -- focusing on memory errors
Compile-time (syntax) errors, runtime errors (exceptions), and logic errors -- this lesson focuses on runtime errors/exceptions
Apex errors, Java errors, and Python errors -- focusing on Apex errors
Only two categories exist: compile-time and runtime
questions.explain: The lesson names all three categories -- structurally invalid code rejected before running, valid code that fails while executing, and valid-and-running code that still produces the wrong result -- and states this lesson covers the middle category, exceptions.

questions.q: What happens to any remaining lines inside a `try` block after an exception is thrown partway through it?
options: They are skipped entirely -- execution immediately jumps to a matching catch block
They run anyway, after the catch block finishes
They run first, before the catch block
Apex restarts the entire try block from the top
questions.explain: The lesson states that the moment an exception is thrown, execution immediately jumps out of the try block into a matching catch block, skipping any remaining lines in the try block after the failure point.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when does a `finally` block run?
options: Only if an exception was thrown
Only if no exception was thrown
Always, after the try/catch finishes, whether or not an exception occurred -- making it the right place for cleanup logic
Only if the catch block explicitly calls it
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that finally always runs after try/catch, regardless of outcome, which is exactly why it's suited to cleanup logic that must happen either way.

questions.q: What naming convention does Salesforce use for custom exception classes, per this lesson?
options: The class name must start with the word Exception
The class name must end in the word 'Exception', such as InvalidDiscountException
The class name must match the method that throws it exactly
Custom exception classes cannot have names at all
questions.explain: The lesson states the convention directly: a custom exception class's name should end in 'Exception' -- InvalidDiscountException, not InvalidDiscount -- and shows this created by extending the built-in Exception class.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe a catch block that does nothing meaningful as 'categorically worse' than not catching the exception at all?
options: Because it causes a compile-time error
Because an empty catch block hides a genuine problem by turning a visible failure into a silent one, whereas an uncaught exception at least loudly signals that something is wrong
Because Apex forbids empty catch blocks and will refuse to compile them
Because it always slows down the program significantly
questions.explain: The lesson's anti-pattern warning is precisely this: an empty or non-meaningful catch block silences a real failure instead of surfacing or fixing it, which is worse than an uncaught exception that at least makes the problem visible.
